WITHDREW the dollar figure '$51-94 becomes roughly $177-325'. 3.46 is 270 experimental attempts over 78 experimental runs; it was applied to a budget covering all 100 runs, the 22 guardrail runs were never expanded into attempts, and an attempt multiplier is not a dollar multiplier. No revised dollar range is available. Also withdrew 'the definition is forced by the arithmetic': arithmetic rules out one reading, it does not select full factorial coverage over the cheaper designs now listed in CR-002.

CORRECTED the worked example. It said a D cell's planned denominator is 3 and required 3/3; the run plan says 12 (4 tasks x 3 repetitions). Three is the repetition count, left over from before CR-002 made the attempt the unit. The denominator is always the run plan's planned_attempts for that cell.

The published tie-break (delta, passes, smaller variance, condition) named a variance term that aggregate.select_strongest did not implement, so document and code disagreed on any tie. The sort key now carries variance; absent variance sorts last rather than as zero, which would win every tie.
